title: Impact: order_total takes the VAT rate from settings
subtitle: What changes when `pricing.order_total` stops using the `VAT_RATE` constant and takes `settings.vat_rate` (`ACME_VAT_RATE`) as a parameter, and the order to make it in.

verdict.text: **Not safe as one step: it needs 4 deploys.** A required `vat_rate` breaks 3 static call sites, 1 dynamic one in `report.py` (it fails only when the report runs) and 4 tests. The bigger risk is the money: `settings.vat_rate` has been loaded since the first commit but **never read**. Wiring it in makes whatever value each environment holds live in the totals that finance sums, so check that value and tell finance before callers switch.

blocks.text:
`pricing.order_total(order)` becomes `pricing.order_total(order, vat_rate)`. Callers pass `settings.vat_rate`, which `config.load_settings` reads from `ACME_VAT_RATE`, then `vat_rate` in `acme.yaml`, then the default `"0.20"`. The `VAT_RATE` constant in `pricing.py` goes away. [high]

`order_total` never reads `VAT_RATE` itself: it calls `vat_total(order)`, and that function reads the constant. So `vat_total` must take the rate too. If it doesn't, the total uses the setting while the report's VAT column (`vat_total`) keeps 0.20, and the two disagree. [high]

blocks.title: The setting has never been read
blocks.text: `Settings.vat_rate` (`config.py:14`, `:28`) has existed since `0b4eca9` (2026-05-04), and `acme.yaml` support since `4f04522` (2026-07-20). No code reads `settings.vat_rate` (grep finds no `.vat_rate` read). So until now, setting `ACME_VAT_RATE` has had no effect. After the change, any value other than 0.20 in an environment variable or an `acme.yaml` changes stored totals, receipts and reports from the next run. [high]

items: **`orders.total_cents`** is computed once at import time with the hard-coded 0.20 (`storage.py:31-32`). There is no schema change and no new field to read, so old rows stay readable. [high]

**Rows don't record the rate.** If an environment holds a rate other than 0.20, rows from before and after the deploy use different rates and nothing shows it. Finance's per-day `SUM(total_cents)` mixes them. [high]

**Re-imports rewrite history.** `INSERT OR REPLACE` recomputes an old order with the current rate. The cron re-ran the 2026-10-02 file on 2026-10-03 (`logs/acme-orders.log:28`), so re-runs do happen. If the rate ever changes, re-importing an old export silently changes old totals. [high]

**Writes by position.** `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)` (`storage.py:31`) names no columns. If you later decide to store the rate per order, name the columns first. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` won't add a column to an existing file, so that also needs an `ALTER TABLE`. This change doesn't require it. [high]

**Configuration counts as stored data here.** `ACME_VAT_RATE` and `acme.yaml` (gitignored) live in each environment, not in the repo. Their values have never had any effect, so nobody has had a reason to keep them correct. [high] There is no `.dockerignore`, so the Dockerfile's `COPY . .` would bake a local `acme.yaml` into the image, and `load_settings` reads `acme.yaml` from the working directory `/srv/acme-orders`. [med]
YAML parses `vat_rate: 0.20` as the float 0.2. `str()` turns it into `"0.2"` and then `Decimal("0.2")`, the same value, and `_round` quantizes the result, so there's no drift. [high]

items.title: The report's dynamic `getattr` call has no test
items.evidence: `daily_report` builds `discount_total`, `vat_total` and `order_total` by name and calls each with `(order)`. Once the parameter is required, it raises `TypeError` only when someone runs `report`. While the parameter has a default, it silently uses 0.20. No test calls `daily_report`.
items.fix: Before moving the callers, add a test: with a given rate, the `vat` and `total` columns use that rate and `total = subtotal - discount + vat`, rounded.

items.title: Nothing tests the import path to `total_cents`, the value finance sums
items.evidence: `cli import → import_file → save_order → orders.total_cents`. `test_importer.py` covers only `parse_amount` and `read_orders`.
items.fix: Test `import_file(path, db, vat_rate)` against a temporary SQLite file and assert on `total_cents` for a known order at 0.20 and at another rate.

items.title: No test covers `load_settings`'s order of precedence or checks its range
items.evidence: No test checks that the environment overrides `acme.yaml`, which overrides the default, or how a YAML float is parsed. Any `Decimal` is accepted, including `20` or a negative rate.
items.fix: Add tests for the three sources, and reject rates outside 0 ≤ rate < 1 when loading.

items.title: `cli.main` `check` and `import --notify` have no test
items.evidence: Nothing proves that the CLI passes `settings.vat_rate` and not the default.
items.fix: Test `main(["check", file])` with `ACME_VAT_RATE` set, and `--notify` with `requests.post` mocked, asserting on the total that is sent.

items.title: Pricing has only been tested at 0.20
items.evidence: All 4 tests rely on the constant. No rate other than 0.20 has ever run through `order_total` or `vat_total`.
items.fix: Add cases at 0.10 and at `Decimal("0.2")` vs `Decimal("0.20")`, including the case where rounding happens once per order.

sections.title: Safe order
sections.intro: Expand, settle the setting, move the callers, then contract. Each step is one deploy and has a check that must pass before the next.

blocks.title: The import is already failing
blocks.text: Every 06:00 import since 2026-10-02 has exited with `decimal.InvalidOperation` (`logs/acme-orders.log:10`, `:29`). The cause is `49bc16d` (Jon Berg, 2026-09-30), which removed `.replace(",", ".")` from `parse_amount`, while the export contains `12,50` (`data/orders-2026-10-02.csv:7`). `report.read_adjustments` has the same problem with `-8,40`. That's not part of this change, but the checks in step 3 need a working import, so fix it first and give the fix a regression test. [high]

items.title: 1. Expand: add the parameter with the old value as its default
items.text: `vat_total(order, vat_rate=VAT_RATE)` and `order_total(order, vat_rate=VAT_RATE)`, with `order_total` passing the rate on to `vat_total`. Don't change any callers yet. Add the pricing tests at other rates. **Check:** the 4 existing tests pass unchanged, and `acme-orders check` on a sample export prints the same totals before and after.

items.title: 2. Settle the setting and tell finance
items.text: Add the range check and the `load_settings` tests. On every environment (the `/srv/acme-orders` cron host, the Docker image, CI), find `ACME_VAT_RATE` and any `acme.yaml`, and confirm the value is 0.20 or agree on a different one. Tell finance-ops@example.com before step 3, as docs/finance-export.md asks. **Check:** on the production host, `python -c "from acme_orders.config import load_settings; print(load_settings().vat_rate)"` prints the agreed rate.

items.title: 3. Move the callers
items.text: `cli.py:32` and `:36` pass `settings.vat_rate`. `import_file(path, db, vat_rate)`, called from `cli.py:29`. `daily_report(..., vat_rate=...)`, called from `cli.py:39`, with the `getattr` loop replaced by explicit calls. Add the report, import and CLI tests. **Check:** after the next 06:00 import, `storage.totals_by_day` for the day equals the sum of the `check` output for that file. One order checked through `GET /orders/<id>` matches, and in the report, total = subtotal − discount + VAT.

items.title: 4. Contract: make it required and remove the constant
items.text: Make `vat_rate` required on `order_total` and `vat_total`, delete `VAT_RATE`, and pass `Decimal("0.20")` in `tests/test_pricing.py`. Do this only after the owners confirm nothing outside the repo imports `acme_orders.pricing`. From then on, a missed caller fails with a `TypeError` instead of silently using 0.20. **Check:** grep finds no `VAT_RATE`, the tests pass, and `import`, `check` and `report` each run once on a sample file.

blocks.text: Later, and only if the rate is expected to change: store the rate with each order (named-column `INSERT` first, then `ALTER TABLE`), or pick the rate by order date, so that re-importing an old export can't rewrite its totals. [med]
